A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain 24 readable pages. Text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original Rastrigin optimization experiments, including empirical probabilities and objective-value summaries in Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–3.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original Rastrigin experiments and reports additional median outcomes in Table 1.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2, the Langevin dynamics, discretization, and Gaussian update formulas are unchanged. Algorithm 2 is relocated within Section 4.2.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Rastrigin benchmark and 10- and 20-dimensional evaluation scenarios. Appendix A retains the same one- and two-dimensional illustrations; no dataset or task coverage is added.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains comparisons against OLA from Vempala and Wibisono (2019) and ULA from Ma et al. (2021). Table 3 retains SA, FSA, SMC-SA, and CSA, with their baseline scores unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5 retains the same parameter choices, initializations, tolerances, sample counts, and iteration budgets, including the fixed effort N·K = 140000. Added medians do not establish changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: The step-size, inverse-temperature, dimensionality, annealing, and fixed-effort investigations are retained. The added median summaries change statistical reporting without introducing a new diagnostic question, ablation condition, or robustness scenario.

E5.justification: Table 1 newly reports medians alongside means and standard deviations over the same 100 runs. Run counts and uncertainty measures remain unchanged; additional runs, seeds, or significance testing are not reported.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds 12 median values, including 0.329 for h = 0.01 and a = 4. Its mean for h = 0.1 and a = 2 changes from 6.9790 to 6.970, beyond ordinary rounding. Other table edits mainly reduce decimal precision; Table 3 and all plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Assumption 2.2 is reformulated for the marginal Gibbs measure instead of the joint measure. Remark 2.3 adds explicit tensorization constants and a bounded-perturbation lower bound, whereas v3 discusses these qualitatively. The core convergence statements and appendix assumptions and proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about oracle-based global optimization, the high-resolution Langevin sampler, and Rastrigin performance. Remark 4.7 still acknowledges that the proved rates do not improve existing Langevin bounds.

C2.justification: Remark 2.3 extends the earlier dimension-dependence discussion with explicit potentially exponential dependence on inverse temperature a. Section 5 now connects the observed slowdown at larger a to this dependence. The existing open questions and acceleration qualification remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The code-access footnote changes the repository path from GlobalOptimization to Global-Optimization. Python 3.8 and the disclosed implementation parameters are retained; no underlying code change is established.

R1.justification: The introduction expands and qualifies the relationship to Nesterov acceleration, distinguishing convex and strongly convex guarantees. It adds Attouch et al. (2018) and removes the Nesterov (1983) reference; the broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites expand the introduction and Remark 2.3, with smaller experimental-prose and spelling edits. Publication and review information is added, while the section and appendix organization remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains median rows, several captions become more descriptive, and figures, tables, and Algorithm 2 move relative to surrounding text. Publication headers are added. All six figures retain identical underlying images.

improvement.justification: The medians and editorial clarifications provide limited benefits, but Remark 2.3 introduces an incorrect Gaussian log-Sobolev coefficient absent from v3. Its rho_b = 1/b fails Equation (3) for b < 1: shifted Gaussians with variance 1/b require rho_b ≤ b. This weakens mathematical reliability in a primarily theoretical paper and outweighs the modest reporting gains. The unchanged core algorithms and proofs limit the deterioration.
